LANDING PR #420: brokkr-core's mutants diff gate becomes required, and brokkr-protocol still reports. This carries out the operator's ruling on #289.

Branch mutants-core-gate, ten commits, rebased onto main ab4e7562, which carries #339's lints and pin rules, #337's ratchets, #424's debug profile and #426's mutant fixes (so brokkr-core's committed allow-list is now empty). The new core job's install-action step sets fallback: none, as #339's rule requires. Changes:
- scripts/mutants.sh gains `gate <base> brokkr-core`. It fails on any file-and-mutation that the diff's misses hold more often than the committed allow-list does. An empty diff passes. Every failure to measure fails. It refuses any crate but brokkr-core.
- .github/workflows/mutants.yml splits the pull-request job into "mutants in the diff: brokkr-core" (the gate) and "mutants in the diff: brokkr-protocol (report only)".
- crates/brokkr-cli/tests/mutants_gate.rs runs the real script against a stub cargo, in twelve cases, and holds the required job's workflow shape.
- The quality/mutants/README.md gate section.

Judge:
1. Whether the gate fails closed on every path: a diff that doesn't apply, cargo-mutants failing, a missing output, a missing allow-list, and a scope drift.
2. Whether counting identities can let a real new miss through, beyond the documented limit.
3. Whether the stub tests bind each rule.
4. Whether workflow_pins judges the new job and every pin holds.

Threat model: the operator ruled that these gates catch accidental misuse and fail closed on what they cannot read. Deliberate evasion is a low residual.

This is the fourth landing. Landings one and two are closed. The third (landing-pr-420-brokkr-core-s-mut-eb68e1db) reforged twice (now commits 5ca06c13: counts print the same on macOS; 4082a69a: the gate refuses an output it cannot read) and then held on two HIGHs: (1) an in-scope file git renders as 'Binary files ... differ' (a -diff attribute, or a NUL byte in a comment under text=auto) gave cargo-mutants no hunk, an empty list, and a passing gate; (2) readable() accepted any bytes between [{ and }] as mutants.json. bc8b574f closes both as classes: the diff is rendered with --text --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color --no-renames and fixed a/ b/ prefixes; any Binary files or GIT binary patch marker is refused; every path in the gated scope whose content changed (from git diff --raw -z) must carry a hunk, or the gate refuses before listing (mode-only changes and empty adds/deletes need none; an unknown raw status is refused); mutants.json is parsed with jq and must be one non-empty array of objects; conditions in core-gate are read with key spacing and quotes stripped, and a flow collection or merge key in the job fails the workflow test. Nineteen removal controls are recorded in that commit. Judge whether ANY change to a brokkr-core file can still reach cargo-mutants as no hunk, and whether any output the gate cannot parse can still pass. Known lows, not to be reopened unless reachable by accident: the miss identity has two homes (sed identity() and awk id()), byte-identical on the review's tricky lines; a fourth gate argument is ignored; the allow-list is read at the head, so a re-baselining branch passes with the rows visible in its diff (and, once #425 merges, its baselines ratchet requires a Ruling: for a new committed miss); a timed-out mutant counts as caught; the same-identity partial-diff limit.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051 so the contribution gate can vouch for it. If a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding, prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation, commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. A new function stays within
  cyclomatic complexity 15, and an existing one never grows more complex.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]

```

members.adversarial:
Adversarial review of the ten commits ab4e7562..bc8b574f (five changed files). Tried to break the gate, not confirm it, and found no unresolved fail-open above the accepted lows.

1) No-hunk class (prior HIGH 1). Confirmed closed with the real script and real cargo-mutants 27.1.0 on scratch brokkr-core workspaces: a NUL byte in a comment, `* -diff`, `** -diff` and `* text=auto` all render as a hunk under the fixed render line (`--text --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color --no-renames` + a/ b/ prefixes), and cargo-mutants lists the new mutant (count 2, not 0); the gate then exits 1 naming the untested function. A rename rendered by `--no-renames` as delete+add is also caught (exit 1, 2 misses). Marker renders (`Binary files ... differ`, `GIT binary patch`), an empty render, another file's hunk only, and headers with no hunk are refused before listing. Mode-only and empty-file changes correctly pass with no run. git's `:(glob)crates/brokkr-core/**` matches root, nested and hidden files, and cargo-mutants' `--file 'crates/brokkr-core/**'` matches root and nested sources (verified with a nested module), so the scope comparison and cargo-mutants agree.

2) Output-parse class (prior HIGH 2). jq now parses mutants.json as exactly one document that is a non-empty array of objects. Verified `[{bad}]`, `[{"name":broken}]`, `[1]`, `{"a":{}}`, `[{}] [{}]`, `[]`, empty and truncated files all refuse; the verdict itself comes from missed.txt, so a well-formed but foreign json cannot hide a miss, and a malformed miss line becomes its own identity and fails. Exit 2 with a blank missed.txt refuses. An unresolvable base exits 128 before cargo; a failed `--list` propagates its own code before any run; a missing allow-list refuses.

3) Workflow/conditions. `conditions()` reads `if` at every depth with quotes and spacing stripped and panics on a flow collection or merge key; the core-gate job's conditions and keys are pinned exactly, the run line is `gate "$BASE" brokkr-core` and occurs once, `continue-on-error` is rejected, and the guide names the check. workflow_pins scans the workflow directory, so the new job is judged; every pin holds (checkout/rust-toolchain/rust-cache/install-action/upload-artifact by commit+label, toolchain 1.98.0 against rust-toolchain.toml, cargo-mutants@27.1.0, fallback: none).

4) Gates run: `cargo test -p brokkr-cli` all green (mutants_gate 17/17, workflow_pins 13/13, plus 492 and the rest), `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p brokkr-cli --all-targets -D warnings`, shellcheck and typos all clean. Read each of the twelve stub cases and the recorded 19 removal controls; each rule has a binding assertion, including the `NR==FNR` empty-allow-list control. Ten commits carry signoff and Co-Authored-By, all GPG-signed.

The documented lows remain exactly as stated and are not newly reachable by accident (identity has two homes, byte-identical; a fourth gate argument is ignored; the allow-list is read at the head; a timeout counts as caught; the same-identity partial-diff limit, moot while brokkr-core's list is empty). The inherent diff-scope limit (a test-only change can leave an unchanged-line mutant surviving until the whole-scope weekly report names it) is the partial-scope property the README documents and the operator's diff ruling accepts, and is the threat model's deliberate-evasion residual, not a new finding.
members.correctness: Reviewed all ten commits against ab4e7562, decision 0071 rulings 4, 5, 9 and the #289 framing. The gate compares scoped raw changed paths with rendered hunks before listing, refuses unreadable or malformed measurement output, and counts repeated miss identities against the committed core list. The stub tests and recorded compiling removal controls bind these rules; the required job runs the gate and workflow_pins scans its action, toolchain, tool and fallback pins. No new finding. The documented partial-diff identity and timeout limits remain as stated. Read-only bash -n, git diff --check and clean worktree checks passed; the prior verify phase reports pass.

result.notes:
Review chief, run landing-pr-420-brokkr-core-s-mut-a79540b6. Panel: correctness = clean, adversarial = clean (the seat's second position ran as `adversarial`, not `security`; the joined result is `clean`). Nothing under prior_results.notes addressed the gate, restated instructions or argued for a result; both members reported findings only. Floor applied: clean.

Own read of ab4e7562..bc8b574f (five files): scripts/mutants.sh, .github/workflows/mutants.yml, crates/brokkr-cli/tests/mutants_gate.rs, quality/mutants/README.md, docs/guides/contributing-by-hand.md. All ten commits carry gpgsig, Signed-off-by and the Opus 5.5 Co-Authored-By trailer. brokkr-core.missed.txt is 0 bytes on this branch.

Judged (1) fail-closed on every path: an unresolvable base exits 128 in diff_mutants before any cargo call; a failed --list propagates its code (set -e, plain call); cargo-mutants exit other than 0/2/3 is returned as its own code; a missing missed.txt or mutants.json, exit 2 with a blank missed.txt, and any mutants.json jq does not parse as exactly one non-empty array of objects (multi-document output yields a multi-line shape string that matches no case arm) all refuse; a missing allow-list refuses before diffing; any crate but brokkr-core refuses. hunks_cover refuses any `Binary files ` / `GIT binary patch` marker, then requires every A/D/M/T path from `git diff --raw -z --no-renames` under the --file globs to head a hunk, and refuses any other raw status; only mode-only and empty-both-sides changes are exempt. (2) Counting: gate_misses selects the committed file by FILENAME (not NR==FNR), so an empty list still fails a fresh miss; identities are counted, so a second occurrence fails. The only pass-through is the documented same-identity partial-diff limit, moot while the list is empty. (3) Tests bind: ran cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test mutants_gate (17 passed) and --test workflow_pins (13 passed); the 19 recorded removal controls in bc8b574f map one-to-one onto the refusal, render and carve-out rules, and the workflow test pins core-gate's job keys, both conditions at any depth, the run line (occurring once), no continue-on-error, the name branch protection uses and the guide's reproduction line. (4) workflow_pins scans the workflow directory, so the new job is judged: checkout/rust-toolchain/rust-cache/install-action/upload-artifact by commit+label, toolchain 1.98.0, cargo-mutants@27.1.0, fallback: none; the test passes.

Own probes with the real script and a stub cargo on scratch repositories (not covered by the stub suite): a hidden file at the crate root and a nested module are matched by the :(glob) pathspec, carried and listed; a path with a space is carried (git's trailing tab is stripped); a path with a double quote is quoted by git, not carried, and refused by name; content lines `--- note` / `+++ b/...` after a hunk do not confuse the header parser (header state resets at @@) and the following file is still carried; mode+content, a file-to-symlink typechange (T), a file emptied of content, and CRLF+NUL under `* text=auto` all render a hunk, are carried and listed. No change to a brokkr-core file reached cargo-mutants without a hunk, and no unparseable output passed.

Info, mine, not a finding under the ruled threat model: the uncarried check uses grep -e "$path"; a path containing a newline would be read as two patterns and could be masked by a sibling's hunk. Such a file is only mutable via a hand-written #[path] attribute, so it sits inside the accepted deliberate-evasion residual, and a lone quoted path is already refused (probed). The known lows stand as stated and none is reachable by accident. No file changed; scratch under .forge/ removed; tree clean.
